text:
To demonstrate the performance of the [R_cycle_detected](src/main/duplicate.c) function, when the RHS (child argument) is exceptionally large or repetative, then this will cause a large amount of time spent confirming no cycle is detected.

R_cycle_detected is called from R_FixupRHS, which is found
about 8 times within the codebase:

- installAttrib (src/main/attrib.c)
- DO_FAST_SETVECELT (src/main/eval.c)
- SimpleListAssign (src/main/subassign.c)
- do_subassign2_dflt (src/main/subassign.c)
- do_subassign3_dflt (src/main/subassign.c 3 times)

```cache <- function(n) {
  structure(
    list(
      num = sample(1e6, n, TRUE),
      let = sample(letters, n, TRUE),
      tree = ape::rtree(n)
    ),
    class = "cache"
  )
}

large_cache <- lapply(
  seq_len(1000),
  cache
)
slow_vec <- function(num, caches) {
  structure(num, caches = caches, class = "slow_vec")
}
print.slow_vec <- function(x, ...) {
  cat("slow_vec with", length(attr(x, "caches")), "caches\n")
  invisible(x)
}
v <- slow_vec(1, large_cache)

lst <- lapply(
  seq_len(50000),
  function(i) {
    sample(1e3, 10) |>
      slow_vec(large_cache)
  }
)```
slow to set as an attribute

```y <- structure(1, foo = "")
system.time(attr(y, "foo") <- lst)
#>    user  system elapsed
#>   5.813   0.016   5.830```
The R_cycle_detect function must iterate through all of the data, as well each attribute recursively to check if the RHS contains, the LHS. This can be expensive to do as seen above, especially if the list structure contains the same object. This can be resolved by using the hashmap implementation within the code base to track the addresses as the function walks the RHS, being that if the address already exists in the map, then we know that the object has been checked and we can return early from recursing.

This is a contrived example but is inspired by some work i’ve been doing with the vctrs package, in which it is easy to ‘chop’ a vector into a list by which each element contains very similar attributes.

I don’t have a working example in C yet, but i’ve been iterating an example in Zig, and it seems to work well. In my work i was creating lists of vctrs that would cause R_cycle_detected to run for 30 seconds (in experimenting I confirmed with my data structure R_cycle_detected was being called over 2 billion times :sweat_smile:)
